## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Two things need fixing. `slugify` removes non-ASCII letters, so titles in other scripts become wrong or empty slugs, and the PR description has no `## Testing` section, which the project policy requires. This review read `AGENTS.md`, the PR title and body, the full diff, and both new files at the PR head. It traced `slugify` against the four parametrized test cases and against non-ASCII input. Collapsing runs of separators and trimming hyphens at the ends work as described and are tested by the `"  Already--hyphenated  "` and `"---"` cases.

## Changes
The PR adds `app/slug.py` with a `slugify(title)` helper that lowercases a title, replaces runs of characters outside `[a-z0-9]` with one hyphen, and trims hyphens from the ends. It also adds a parametrized test in `tests/test_slug.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — Handle non-ASCII letters in slugify — For `"Café"`, `slugify` returns `"caf"`, and for `"日本語"` it returns `""`, because `[^a-z0-9]+` treats every non-ASCII letter as a separator. The PR body says the function replaces "runs of non-alphanumeric characters", but `é` and CJK characters are alphanumeric (`"é".isalnum()` is `True`), so the code is narrower than the description. No test covers non-ASCII input. — Pages with titles that are fully non-Latin get an empty slug, and every such page maps to the same URL; accented titles lose letters and can collide (`"Café"` and `"Caf"` both become `"caf"`). — Fix: Choose one behavior and test it: keep Unicode letters with `re.sub(r"[\W_]+", "-", title.lower())`, or transliterate first (for example, NFKD-normalize and drop combining marks) and decide what an empty result should become. Then update the PR body to match.
- PR body — correctness — Add the required `## Testing` section — The PR description is one paragraph and has no `## Testing` section. `AGENTS.md:4` says: "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." — Reviewers cannot tell from the description whether or how the new helper and its tests were run, which the project policy requires.
